name: Phone ad — colour-block grammar (spec)
note: Modelled on the iPhone 5C campaign: flat saturated colour, the product in hand, and hard fast cuts snapping between the two. Bright and graphic, the opposite of the black-and-slow product film. A SPEC piece — no Apple footage, logo or typeface.
not_official: Concept work from Creative Commons stock. Never to be presented as an Apple advertisement.
subject: a smartphone held in a hand
a face lit by a screen
someone taking a photograph
a glowing screen in the dark
a macro close-up of a surface
a studio product shot on black
subject_variety_note: Raised from 0.10. With it low the chooser simply never left the phone: 20 product shots and 0 colour blocks, because the phone clips also fit the brightness and saturation ranges best. The grammar is product/colour/product -- alternation is the form, not a side effect.
budgets_note: Fast. The 5C spots cut about every half-bar and never hold. max_shot_s of 2.2 is the ceiling that keeps it snapping.
prefers_note: Bright and saturated -- the inverse of every range in ad-iphone18pro.json, which is the point of keeping taste in a file.
subject_note: The colour fields land under "a macro close-up of a surface" -- without that phrase the brief asked only for phones and the grammar lost half its alphabet: 12 product shots and 0 colour blocks.
salience_floor_note: Low enough to reach half-bar cuts, which is what makes this grammar snap.
